title: chat: bridge host-owned Microsoft credentials to Copilot
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

-->

Builds on #345132. This is the credential-bridge layer of the Copilot account-choice MVP; review against `copilot-m365/rollout`.

## Changes

- Capture one startup-effective Microsoft bridge gate for the Agent Host. Live setting updates remain requests for the next host start.
- Connect the supported SDK `entra.tokenProvider` to existing AHP authentication and VS Code's default Microsoft account. Keep `CopilotClient`, `RuntimeConnection.forStdio`, and the separate runtime process.
- Bind the account, resource and scopes; try silent acquisition before existing same-account interactive recovery. Withdraw authority on sign-out/disconnect and reject late credentials. A window that has not supplied credentials cannot revoke another window's authority merely because its own default account differs.
- Publish changing credential requirements independently of the model catalog. Keep ordinary GitHub and gate-off behavior unchanged; add no token store or AHP wire fields.

No dependency bump or rollout activation. SDK: `1.0.27-unstable.41214319014.g4f70995`; bundled runtime: `1.0.103-unstable.r41214319014.g4f70995`.

## Draft boundary

**This is infrastructure, not an end-to-end usable Microsoft account-choice flow.** Current setup still establishes a GitHub default account; later setup/discovery work must supply the intended Microsoft identity and initiate the runtime account flow. This PR does not implement service discovery/selection, active-context readiness, merged catalogs, session migration or billing changes.

Real Microsoft sign-in/renewal, EMU exchange, M365 entitlement and inference remain unverified. The MVP uses existing `required`/`expired` recovery rather than promising silent-only recovery or forced cache bypass; no new AHP cancellation flow is introduced.

## Review passes

Completed code-style, code-review and disposable/lifecycle review. Fixed missing-token recovery, cross-window revocation, session/account ID conflation, stale resource publication, same-token session provenance and credential completion after revocation; added regression tests.

Measured cyclomatic complexity with ESLint and cognitive complexity with SonarJS 4.2.2, using temporary tooling outside the checkout. All newly introduced production functions are at most **12 cyclomatic / 7 cognitive** (review limits: 15/15). Existing above-limit methods were compared with the rollout baseline and their small integration deltas reviewed; this is not a claim that the entire files meet those limits, and unrelated legacy methods were not refactored.

## Validation

All commands below passed on Windows with Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.16.0:

```powershell
pnpm run build-fast --client-only
pnpm run typecheck-client

.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotEntraAuthentication.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentConfigurationService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostClientConnectionService.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostAuth.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\copilotEntraAuthentication.test.ts --reporter dot
# 192 passing

.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgent.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\protocolServerHandler.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentSideEffects.test.ts --grep "authentication|authenticate|credential|GitHub|startup Microsoft|protected resources" --reporter dot
# 181 passing

.\scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotEntraAuthentication.integrationTest.ts --reporter spec
# 2 passing: the transport contract plus the runner's registry guard

$files = @(git diff --name-only -- '*.ts'); $files += @(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- '*.ts'); pnpm run eslint @files
# Passed on all 25 changed TypeScript files before commit
pnpm run valid-layers-check
# Module and type-layer checks passed
git --no-pager diff --check
```

The integration test uses a real loopback WebSocket AHP connection, the host protocol handler/authentication controller/adapter, the installed SDK and a separate native stdio runtime. A synthetic Graph credential establishes the host identity; the runtime requests its actual EMU scope, then the client withdraws authority and the runtime stops. Surrounding agent services are fixtures. No synthetic resource token is sent to Microsoft/GitHub and no personal credentials are used. **This is negative transport/lifecycle evidence, not successful authentication or entitlement evidence.**

Earlier isolated Code OSS checks verified that live setting edits, window reload and a second connected window preserve the host's effective gate; a restarted app reads the saved request and installs the real SDK callback. Those checks did not sign in. Test processes, profiles and helpers were cleaned up. Full repository suites and positive authenticated journeys were not run.

title: chat: add accessible previews for inline GitHub references
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Adds on-demand detail previews for inline GitHub issue and pull request references in the Chat composer, using the existing chat reference card renderer. Inspect the title, status, description, and branches without leaving the composer or submitting the draft.

Related: #334061.

Click a reference, or highlight it with arrow keys and press Enter, to open its card. Hovering and ordinary arrow navigation leave details closed so they don't interrupt composing. Inside the card, the linked issue or pull request number opens the referenced item separately; branch buttons copy their names. Existing chat reference surfaces continue to use hover previews.

## Proposed interaction

**Native Windows Agents window, Dark 2026:** hover stays quiet; click opens details; Tab reaches the Open link; Escape returns to the same draft. The second half shows Enter activation, links and branch-copy controls, and Tab returning to composing.

[Watch the 20-second mouse and keyboard interaction](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e5030cf-109b-472c-a841-d75de60d29a5)

The recording is cropped around the card and composer, runs at normal speed, and keeps captions outside the UI.

## Accessibility

- A named, nonmodal reference preview exposes its expanded state and moves focus to the first available link. Loading content has a named focus target until links arrive.
- Tab and Shift+Tab traverse links and copy controls. Escape or either Tab boundary dismisses the card and restores composer focus; a card without controls also has a keyboard exit.
- Accessible View presents the details as text, and Accessibility Help explains previewing, opening, and returning to the draft. Closing either restores the invoking control, or the first link if loading has completed. Composer refreshes retain the preview's DOM owner while reading and apply its pending widget update when the card is dismissed.
- Unavailable details keep a keyboard-reachable Open link. Removing a reference, changing accounts, or rerendering doesn't leave focus in detached content or reopen a dismissed preview.

**High-contrast keyboard focus:** the Open Pull Request link remains visibly focused against the card and composer.

![Keyboard focus on the reference-opening link in High Contrast Dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/509dab27-7b42-475d-8d2a-606bb8d09e4a)

**Unavailable details:** the card still offers an Open action instead of leaving the user stuck in an empty popup.

![Unavailable reference details with a focused Open link and the unchanged composer draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35239f8c-f934-412d-b967-400d82b866c4)

Validated with native Windows keyboard navigation, default light/dark and both high-contrast themes, 207% zoom, and reduced motion. Actual NVDA 2026.3 generated utterances were captured for the title, status, description, control names, Accessible View/help, and ordinary focus return. For example, `Open Pull Request #343576` is announced as a link, and `Copy Base Branch main` as a button. Accessible View content was read through NVDA's actual caret Say All, not supplied speech. Additional loading-completion and production rerender combinations passed native app-scoped checks and regression tests; those combinations weren't rechecked with NVDA.

Audio playback and native screen-reader behavior on other operating systems weren't tested. External navigation and branch copying are verified at the opener/clipboard callbacks; the recording doesn't launch an external browser.

## How to test

1. Sign in to GitHub and turn on `chat.inlineAttachments.enabled`. Paste an accessible issue or pull request URL into an unsent Chat draft, for example https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/343576.
2. Hover the resulting reference and move through it with arrow keys. Details should stay closed.
3. Click the reference, or highlight it with arrows and press Enter. Inspect its real details, then Tab to the linked number to open the referenced item.
4. Traverse the links and copy controls. Escape, Shift+Tab from the first link, or Tab from the last control should return to the unchanged draft. Clicking the chip again should dismiss its preview.
5. On Windows, use Alt+F2 for Accessible View and Alt+F1 for help while the card has focus. Close either and confirm focus returns to the invoking control.

<details>
<summary>Automated validation</summary>

- `pnpm run compile` — passed, full product compilation.
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed, final client output refreshed.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Complete branch TypeScript lint — passed without warnings:

  ```powershell
  $files = git diff --name-only 18c52617ca765445751c66ffb61137d9101823cc..HEAD
  pnpm run eslint $files
  ```

- `npm run -s precommit` — passed through the commit hook, including formatting/hygiene.
- Focused unit tests — **170 passed**:

  ```powershell
  .\scripts\test.bat --reporter dot `
    --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\input\editor\chatInlineAttachments.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\chatContentParts\chatAttachmentsContentPart.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\github\test\browser\githubResourceDetails.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\platform\hover\test\browser\hoverService.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\workbench\test\browser\chatPillHover.test.ts
  ```

The focused tests cover deliberate activation and draft preservation, first/last/empty-control exits, loading and retry, external-open and copy callbacks, account invalidation, Accessible View/help during loading and rerendering, deferred refresh on dismissal, and unchanged non-inline tooltip and ordinary-hover behavior. Full integration and smoke suites weren't run.

</details>

title: Align RPM dependencies with the mainline Copilot runtime
body:

-->

## Problem

Follow-up to the merged [SDK upgrade #345615](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/345615). Its GitHub CI passed, but full nonpublishing [Product validation 492231](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=492231) detected RPM dependency-reference drift on Linux x64 and arm64. Electron integration and replay CI do not execute this distribution-packaging guard.

The runtime remains SDK `1.0.29-preview.1` / runtime `1.0.106-2`. This PR does not change SDK pins, binaries, permission behavior, test gates, or the dependency-check failure policy.

## Exact change and compatibility assessment

Only `build/linux/rpm/dep-lists.ts` changes: one added reference and two removed references.

| Architecture | Reference change | Binary evidence | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| x64 | Add `libdl.so.2(GLIBC_2.3.3)(64bit)` | Candidate `runtime.node` imports `dlinfo@GLIBC_2.3.3`; baseline does not | Legitimate additional symbol requirement, below the existing glibc 2.28 floor |
| x64 and arm64 | Remove `libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.27)(64bit)` | Baseline `runtime.node` imports `log2f@GLIBC_2.27`; candidate no longer imports it or requires that libm symbol version | Remove an obsolete requirement; no platform-floor increase |

The artifacts were the exact public npm packages for baseline `1.0.27-unstable.41214319014.g4f70995` and candidate `1.0.29-preview.1`, independently packed and inspected with Xcode's LLVM ELF tools. No foreign-platform package was installed into either dependency root. Task-owned downloads were removed afterward.

Both candidate runtime binaries retain a maximum glibc requirement no newer than 2.28, consistent with the runtime's pinned glibc 2.28 toolchains. The existing `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.28)(64bit)` package floor remains. `FAIL_BUILD_FOR_NEW_DEPENDENCIES` remains true.

The complete updated arrays match the actual Product package calculation exactly: **99 x64 requirements and 93 arm64 requirements**. The armhf references are unchanged.

The subsequent `Post-job: Codesign deb & rpm` error in the failed build is a consequence of package preparation stopping before the signing daemon starts, not evidence of a separate signing defect.

## Checks and current status

- Exact complete reference-array comparison with both Product-generated dependency lists: **passed**.
- `pnpm -C build run typecheck`: **passed**.
- `pnpm run eslint build/linux/rpm/dep-lists.ts`: **passed**.
- `git diff --check` and normal signed-commit hygiene hooks: **passed**.
- [GitHub Code OSS CI](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/41586731541), CodeQL, component fixtures and automatic code review: **passed** on `25374fdfec69ff29443122a03c20ecd1ac0824a2`.
- Refreshed current-main acceptance: `AGENT_HOST_TEST_PROFILE=full VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 caffeinate -is pnpm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --jobs 2`: **all six suites passed, 998 passing / 108 existing pending, 517.7s**.
- Refreshed all 25 supplemental SDK/prompt/provider entrypoints with `AGENT_HOST_TEST_PROFILE=full VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 caffeinate -is ./scripts/test-integration.sh --runGlob '**/agentHost/test/node/{copilotSdk*,providerIntegration/*,e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E,e2e/providers/codexAgentHostLive}.integrationTest.js'`: **166 passed, 7 existing pending**.
- SDK-owning, discovery and permission-rule unit suites: **3806 passed, 1 existing pending**. Current-main client and build-tool type checks: **passed**.
- Two preceding local refresh commands encountered wall-clock timeouts while the laptop underwent closed-lid and maintenance sleeps. The power log matched those intervals. The unchanged plugin case passed in an isolated retry, then its full owning suite passed; the complete E2E and supplemental batches subsequently passed with task-bounded sleep prevention. No source, assertion, deadline or test gate was changed to obtain those passes.
- [Full Product build 492266](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=492266) and [fresh cross-platform repeat 492265](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=492265): **running** on the final follow-up revision. Both disable publishing/release/step-on-it. Product keeps every shipping target enabled and adds artifact sanity; the CI-mode repeat is supplemental and does not replace distribution packaging.

Product packaging must actually generate the x64/arm64 DEB/RPM packages and run the dependency-reference checks. Windows and macOS E2E jobs were skipped by GitHub's affected-file selection for this build-only follow-up, so the full Product and separate fresh CI-mode run must provide two actual packaged executions on Windows/Linux/macOS.

The SDK upgrade's earlier acceptance included focused Agents Window smoke (5 passing / 5 existing gated pending), native default telemetry export/shutdown checks and an all-eight-platform native audit of 42 changed binaries. These are supplemental evidence, not substitutes for the final packaged Product validation.

The maintainer explicitly deferred the macOS 14 SDK-native deployment floor and the remaining Universe-only fixes. This packaging-only PR neither resolves nor conceals those follow-ups, and makes no macOS 12/13 compatibility claim.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Local harness: reasoning effort of custom-endpoint models is shared globally across windows -- other sessions' GUI still shows the old level while the backend receives the new one
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.73.2026103004 (build 1, prerelease, bundled in Insiders)
- VS Code Version: 1.145.0-insider (commit caeec36b81bb8046f680cfe00d4a6d699b22cd9d)
- OS Version: Windows 10 22H2 (10.0.19045)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent mode, local harness (built-in chat session), custom endpoint (BYOK) model
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): claude-opus-5-5 via a custom endpoint provider (`customendpoint/.../claude-opus-5-5`)
- Logs: not attached -- this issue does not need logs. The repro below is fully deterministic, and the root cause is visible in the source code plus a one-key check in local storage (see "Additional evidence"). Anyone can confirm the behaviour in three steps without collecting any diagnostics.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open a **new VS Code window 1**, open chat, select the **local harness** + the custom-endpoint model `claude-opus-5-5`, set **Thinking Effort = high**, send one message (call this conversation **session A**). Leave the window open.
2. Open a **new VS Code window 2**, select the same local harness + model, set Thinking Effort = high, send one message (conversation **session B**), then change Thinking Effort to **xhigh** and send another message in session B.
3. Go back to **window 1 / session A** (without reloading the window) and send one more message.

**Actual behavior**

- The model picker in window 1 still displays **high** for session A.
- But the request actually sent from session A carries **xhigh**: the local proxy captured the raw HTTP body, and it flips from `output_config: { effort: "high" }` / `reasoning: { effort: "high" }` (before step 2) to `output_config: { effort: "xhigh" }` / `reasoning: { effort: "xhigh" }` (after step 2) for the very same conversation.
- So the reasoning-effort level selected in window 2 silently overrides the level of window 1's conversation, while window 1's UI keeps showing its own stale value. There is no indication in the UI that the outgoing request uses a different level than the one displayed.
- Note: the picker of session A is never touched in this flow -- it is still "high" by the user's explicit choice, yet xhigh goes out on the wire.

**Expected behavior**

- Reasoning effort should be isolated **per conversation/session**: changing it in window 2 must not change what window 1 sends. Session A must keep sending `high` as long as its picker says `high`.
- The displayed level must always equal the level actually sent; if a global value is ever changed under a session's feet, that session must be updated or invalidated, not silently diverge.

**Additional evidence / suspected root cause**

The selected level is persisted in VS Code **global** storage (`<user-data>/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb`), not in per-session chat state:

- Key `chat.modelConfiguration.panel` holds a map keyed only by model id, e.g.
  `{"customendpoint/.../claude-opus-5-5":{"reasoningEffort":"high"}, "customendpoint/.../gemini-3.8-flash-high":{"reasoningEffort":"high"}, ...}`
- Harness-scoped variants exist only for the agent-host harnesses: `chat.modelConfiguration.panel.agent-host-claude`, `.agent-host-codex`, `.agent-host-copilotcli`. The local harness therefore falls into the shared key `chat.modelConfiguration.panel` (scoped only by "panel" location + model id, not by session or window).
- Since that key is window-independent and there is no cross-window change notification for it, window 2's change mutates the value used for new requests in every window, while open chats keep rendering their cached picker state.

**How to verify without logs**

- Steps 1-3 above are enough, and the swap is also visible outside the editor: point the provider at a local proxy and read the raw request body -- the same conversation's `effort` flips from `high` to `xhigh` with no interaction in window 1.
- Purely local check (no network capture needed): after step 2, `<user-data>/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb` contains a single `chat.modelConfiguration.panel` entry for the model id, e.g. `{"customendpoint/.../claude-opus-5-5":{"reasoningEffort":"xhigh"}, ...}` -- there is no session/window dimension in that key, which is why the two conversations cannot hold different levels.

**Impact**

- Multi-window workflows (very common: several workspaces, several chats at once) can send requests at a thinking level the user never chose for that conversation, silently increasing latency/cost or degrading quality.
- It is impossible to run two conversations in parallel with different thinking levels on the same custom-endpoint model.

**Workaround**

- Reload the window (or reopen the chat) after changing the level elsewhere to resync the UI, or duplicate the model entry under different ids if the provider allows it.

title: Fix UTF-16 column counts in TextLength
body:
Fixes #345714.

TextLength.ofText undercounts supplementary Unicode characters because its string iterator yields code points while editor columns use UTF-16 code units. Inserting an emoji and applying the inverse edit leaves a lone surrogate; trimming a completion's common prefix can delete an existing character at a secondary cursor. Count each yielded string's UTF-16 length so inverse ranges and multicursor completions preserve the original text.

Added regressions for UTF-16 length calculation, multiline and multiple-edit inverses, common prefix/suffix reduction, and the actual getSecondaryEdits path. All seven new regressions fail before the fix and pass afterward.

title: TextLength undercounts UTF-16 columns and corrupts inverse and multicursor edits
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: This is reproduced in core tests without loading extensions.

- VS Code Version: source checkout main, version 1.146.0, commit 498770fb016918e2f34e586fc5b26a7342f450a1
- OS Version: macOS 27.2, arm64; Node.js 24.22.1

TextLength.ofText counts supplementary Unicode characters as one column, but editor positions and string offsets use UTF-16 code units. This produces incorrect inverse edit ranges and changes the meaning of edits when their common prefix or suffix is removed.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Build a source checkout with pnpm run build-fast --client-only.
2. Run this from the repository root with node --input-type=module:

~~~js
import './out/vs/editor/common/core/text/positionToOffset.js';
import { TextEdit, TextReplacement } from './out/vs/editor/common/core/edits/textEdit.js';
import { Position } from './out/vs/editor/common/core/position.js';
import { Range } from './out/vs/editor/common/core/range.js';
import { StringText } from './out/vs/editor/common/core/text/abstractText.js';

const source = new StringText('abc');
const edit = TextEdit.insert(new Position(1, 2), '😀');
const updated = edit.apply(source);
console.log(JSON.stringify(edit.inverse(source).applyToString(updated)));
// Actual: "a\ude00bc"; expected: "abc".
console.log(edit.getNewRanges()[0].endColumn);
// Actual: 3; expected: 4.

const prefixSource = new StringText('😀a');
const replacement = new TextReplacement(new Range(1, 1, 1, 4), '😀ab');
const reduced = replacement.removeCommonPrefixAndSuffix(prefixSource);
console.log(reduced.toEdit().apply(prefixSource));
// Actual: "😀b"; expected: "😀ab".
~~~

The inverse deletes only the high surrogate of the inserted emoji. Prefix reduction starts one column early and deletes the existing a. The same mismatch propagates through getSecondaryEdits when accepting an inline completion at multiple cursors: for two lines containing 😀a, cursors at column 4, and a primary replacement of 😀ab, the primary line becomes 😀ab while the secondary line becomes 😀b.

The cause is the for...of string iterator in TextLength.ofText: it yields Unicode code points, while column++ treats each as one UTF-16 unit. Column counts should use the number of UTF-16 units in each yielded string. Newline handling can remain as it is.

title: Windows agent sandbox blocks named pipes, breaking dotnet restore and build and other local IPC tools
body:
Named pipes do not work inside the Windows agent sandbox. Creating a pipe succeeds and it shows up in `\\.\pipe\` enumeration, but connecting fails: a process cannot even connect to a pipe it just created itself. No sandbox setting covers named pipes, so there is no configuration that can grant this.

This breaks any tool that coordinates over local pipes. The common one is the .NET SDK: `dotnet restore` and `dotnet build` on a multi-project solution fail inside the sandbox because MSBuild's default multi-node mode talks to worker processes over `\\.\pipe\MSBuild<PID>`. `dotnet test` fails at its IPC connect the same way. The MSBuild failure is also silent: restore exits with code 1 and no output, which makes it hard to discover that the sandbox is the cause.

Is named-pipe IPC inside the sandbox supported or planned? An allowance scoped to pipes created by processes inside the same sandbox would restore local IPC without exposing host pipes to sandboxed commands.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable the agent sandbox and ask agent to run `dotnet restore` on a multi-project solution inside the sandbox 
2. build exits 1 with no output. The MSBuild communication trace shows the parent's connect to each `\\.\pipe\MSBuild<PID>` failing with `Access to the path is denied` until the build gives up.

## Expected behavior

A sandboxed process can connect to named pipes created by itself or by sibling processes in the same sandbox. Creation already works, so limiting connects to the sandbox's own pipes would keep host pipes protected while allowing local coordination.

## Actual behavior

Multi-node MSBuild restore and build and `dotnet test` fail inside the sandbox. Brief workaround note: `-m:1` forces single-node MSBuild and works, but tools that require pipes have no workaround.

title: Allow Policy Helper registration through VS Code settings
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Let extensions register a Policy Helper for local Copilot Agent Host sessions without a VS Code restart or window reload.

The Agency extension can write `chat.agentHost.copilot.policyHelper` through the configuration API. VS Code forwards the registration to the local Agent Host. The Copilot runtime executes the helper and resolves policy.

Related issue: [github/copilot-agent-runtime#28101](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/issues/28101).

## Extension contract

```ts
await vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('chat.agentHost.copilot').update(
    'policyHelper',
    { path: absoluteHelperPath, args: helperArguments },
    vscode.ConfigurationTarget.Global,
);
```

The setting accepts an executable `path` and optional string `args`. It uses application scope and excludes Settings Sync. The `advanced` tag limits default visibility in the Settings editor. `doNotSuggest: true` omits the key from settings JSON suggestions. The configuration API remains available, and users can inspect the value in raw settings JSON.

An unset, malformed, or whitespace-only path means no helper. Omitted arguments normalize to `[]`. A cleared setting crosses the protocol as an empty-path object, so removal clears the host's previous registration.

## Runtime lifecycle

The normalized registration belongs to the existing client startup snapshot. Addition, removal, path changes, and argument changes trigger the existing safe restart flow. Equivalent registrations do not trigger another restart.

Shared clients wait until active turns, subagents, and credential updates finish. Scoped clients refresh stale configuration at the next idle use. Each runtime launch receives the captured startup value. Change logs report `policyHelper` without its path or arguments.

The next fresh chat receives the helper configuration. Existing chats can retain their previous skill inventory after resume. Helper script content changes do not trigger a restart.

## Policy boundary

A valid registration sets `COPILOT_CLI_POLICY_HELPER` and adds `POLICY_HELPER` to `COPILOT_CLI_ENABLED_FEATURE_FLAGS`. Other feature flags remain intact. An absent registration clears the helper environment variable and adds no helper flag.

Device and server policy remain authoritative. VS Code provides registration, not policy enforcement. This change covers the local Agent Host path only. It does not change the Copilot extension's separate `copilotcli` session path.


The tests cover normalization, registration metadata, removal transport, environment injection, redacted comparisons, captured startup values, scoped clients, and deferred restarts.

An isolated regular Code OSS workbench used a cloned profile and a Windows ARM64 runtime override. The source profile remained untouched.

|---|---|
| Register through an extension with `ConfigurationTarget.Global` | Client restarted automatically without an application relaunch |
| Invoke the generated skill in the next fresh chat | Actual skill invocation returned `policy helper skill for repo devprod.commitlinks` |
| Clear the registration | Client restarted automatically, and a fresh chat reported the skill unavailable |
| Change arguments during an active turn | The skill call completed successfully before the deferred restart |

| Resume a chat that started without the helper | The previous skill inventory remained |

The live run used runtime artifact `70ffdab`, not the bundled runtime. It does not establish published runtime availability. Full integration and smoke suites, remote hosts, and the Agency rollout gate were not exercised.

3. Write the helper registration through the extension configuration API.

5. Invoke the generated skill.
6. During an active turn, change the helper arguments.
7. Confirm that the turn finishes before the client restart.
8. Clear the registration and open a fresh chat.
9. Confirm that the helper skill is absent.

title: Preserve MIME parameter case when values contain slashes
body:
Fixes #345701.

On main, `normalizeMimeType('Multipart/FORM-DATA; boundary="AbC/DeF"')` returns `multipart/form-data; boundary="abc/def"`: the greedy type capture consumes the type/subtype separator and matches a slash inside a quoted parameter instead.

Make the type capture non-greedy so only type/subtype are lowercased and the parameter suffix stays intact, as required by the existing contract and [RFC 2045 §5.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2045#section-5.1). Keeping the original character classes also preserves the existing treatment of invalid types containing line terminators.

Regression coverage exercises both overloads with a boundary, a SOAP action URL, multiple parameters, and invalid types containing LF, CR, U+2028 and U+2029.

Validation:
- Targeted Node MIME suite: **6 passing** (5 MIME tests and the runner's unexpected-error check). The parameter regression was confirmed failing on the original implementation; the line-terminator regression was confirmed failing on the previous PR head.
- Ran `node node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha.js test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --exit --run src/vs/base/test/common/mime.test.ts`.

title: normalizeMimeType lowercases parameter values containing slashes
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Reproduced directly in the core unit tests; no extension is involved. A desktop/Insiders UI reproduction has not been run.

- Source revision: main at 763ca42b86dc21577554c6efd7526903dce082e4
- Test environment: Linux, Node.js v24.22.1

`normalizeMimeType` in `src/vs/base/common/mime.ts` lowercases parameter values when they contain a slash.

For example, calling the helper with:

```ts
normalizeMimeType('Multipart/FORM-DATA; boundary="AbC/DeF"')
```

returns `multipart/form-data; boundary="abc/def"`, but should return `multipart/form-data; boundary="AbC/DeF"`. The strict overload has the same behavior. A quoted SOAP action URL is affected too:

```text
Application/SOAP+XML; action="https://Example.com/Action"
→ application/soap+xml; action="https://example.com/action"
```

The first group in `/^(.+)\/(.+?)(;.+)?$/` is greedy, so the separator can match a slash inside a quoted parameter instead of the type/subtype separator. Part of the parameters then ends up in the groups that are lowercased.

[RFC 2045 §5.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2045#section-5.1) allows quoted parameter values and specifies that boundary values are case-sensitive. The helper's existing comment also says parameters should be preserved.

I have prepared a small fix and a regression test covering both overloads, a boundary, a URL, and multiple parameters. The added test fails on the revision above and passes with the fix.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and this report.

title: Improve readability of function signature tooltips by displaying parameters on separate lines
body:
## Feature Request: Improve readability of function and method signature tooltips

### Problem

When working with functions or methods that have complex or lengthy type definitions, the signature tooltips (parameter hints) can become very difficult to read.

In particular, long return types, template parameters, and parameter types are displayed curtailed on a single line or monochrome, wrapped in ways that make it difficult to distinguish the individual parts of the function signature.

This makes it harder to quickly understand the function's interface, especially in languages with extensive template and type information, such as C++.

See these screenshots for examples:

![VS Code 1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82ee32ea-821a-400f-8ab6-1a45308890a5)

![VS Code 2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6acb6a8-975f-4723-ac16-aaaf77a8547a)

### Proposed solution

I would like to suggest a different layout for function and method signature tooltips:

1. **Use separate lines for individual components:**
   - Return type
   - Function name and template parameters
   - Each function parameter
2. **Dim type information:** Use a less prominent text color for type definitions to visually distinguish them from function and parameter names.
3. **Highlight the active parameter:** When the user is entering a function call, highlight the line corresponding to the currently expected parameter. Type information on this active line should retain its normal brightness rather than being dimmed.

### Example

![VS Code 3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36e38a1e-74b0-48ff-a6d0-85f0e874635f)

The active parameter line would be highlighted, while the remaining lines would be visually subdued.

### Benefits

- Makes complex function signatures easier to scan and understand.
- Improves readability when working with templates and deeply nested types.
- Makes it easier to identify the currently expected argument.
- Reduces the visual complexity of tooltips without sacrificing type information.

This would be particularly beneficial for C++ development, but could also improve the experience in other languages with complex function signatures.

title: it took 2 minutes 24.5 seconds to create the side chat
body:
I was in the middle of typing up a different request in a different session when I was suddenly yanked back into this chat with no real idea why since it had been so long.

## What happened

Creating a side chat with `/btw` took **2 minutes 24.5 seconds**. While creation was pending, I switched to another chat and started typing a prompt. The side chat then opened unexpectedly, interrupting me.

Observed in VS Code Insiders using a remote Agent Host over a tunnel on November 2, 2026.

## Timeline

Times are local, **PST (UTC-08:00)**, on November 2, 2026.

| Time | What happened |
|---|---|
| 7:46:08.872 AM | `/btw` requested a new side chat. |
| 7:46:09.157 AM | The fork path logged a warning that the requested turn was not found in the source session and it would inherit **all 35 turns**. |
| 7:47:08.619 AM | The host explicitly reported the side-chat creation task as **stalled** (`operation=createChat`). |
| 7:47:49-7:48:21 AM | Draft updates confirm I was typing a different prompt in another chat while creation remained pending. |
| 7:48:31.580 AM | The fork reached runtime preparation/resume. |
| 7:48:31.603 AM | SDK session resume started. |
| 7:48:32.103 AM | SDK session resume completed successfully in **500 ms**. |
| 7:48:32.704 AM | The host reported that the forked chat backing had been created. |
| 7:48:33.413 AM | The side-chat creation request completed: **144.541 seconds** after submission. The client immediately subscribed to the new chat. |
| 7:48:34.744 AM | The original `/btw` question was finally sent to the side chat. |

## What took so long?

**Almost the entire delay preceded runtime startup.** Approximately **142.4 seconds** elapsed between the fork warning and runtime preparation. Resuming the runtime itself took only **500 ms**.

| Commit | Change | Tests |

| P13 `0cea06c344f` D1 + D2 | Editors, and the chat, drag between parts and split a part at its edges. Inputs registered as drop targets (the chat input) take every drop on them; new `registerContentDropTarget` for content that handles its center drops (the chat view): editors/groups get the group's edge zones there, other drags are the content's. Parts in the grid ignore part drags. **Move Part Left/Right/Up/Down** (past parts only, never past chrome such as the title row) | `partGrid.test.ts` |
| P15 `4e6a769b7fe` D4 | An editor dropped on a window edge, outside the parts, goes into a new part there, created by the owner's `IPartGridPartFactory`; parts the grid created close with their last editor (also after restore). **Move Editor into New Part Left/Right/Above/Below**. `PartGrid` takes `IEditorGroupsService`. | `partGrid.test.ts` |

The chat in a chat window drags by its session title. The chat view registers as content that handles drops. Shared `getNewWindowBoundsAtDragEnd` (tab drag-out unchanged). | `dnd.test.ts`, `chatWindowDragOut.test.ts`, `chatCompositeBar.test.ts`, `sessionsListChatMoveDnd.test.ts` |

## Review fixes (additive `fixup!` commits)

| Commit | Fixes |
|---|---|
| `a68b1dd7062` (P13) | The view editor's drag handle no longer stops propagation, so the session header adds its session/chat drag data (dragging the header title onto the sessions list or into a chat input works again). |
| `c04ff8320e8` (P15) | Window-edge drops (D4) are decided by the distance to the window edge before card targets, so the top edge and the compact look work; inner drop overlays are disposed. |

| `d75932bb2de` + `b3c7e263aaf` (P16) | D5 follows `workbench.editor.dragToOpenWindow` and the Alt toggle, and only when nothing took the drop; only from the main Agents window. Move Part / Move Editor into New Part announce when there is no part to act on. |

Window edges (D4, Move Part to an edge) are the edges of the parts: the title row keeps spanning the window. |
| `c03a8bc648d` + `60d03ba973a` (P15) | D4 and part-drag window edges are those of the parts: below the title row (an OS drag region across the top of the window, which gets no drag events) and including the outer insets. |
| `cca0884662f` + `1f2a00c7b8b` (P13) | QA BUG-5: over the chat, the edge overlay shows for the drag that creates it and that drag doesn't reach the chat, so the chat doesn't show "Attach File as Context" there. An overlay that shows always takes its drop, even before any drag moved over it. |
| `dd64738b0ad` (P14) | QA BUG-8: Move Part to an edge the part is already at leaves the parts, their sizes and the focus as they are (and announces "already there"). |
| `1009f58fd44` (P16) | The chat leads the window only from the first group of the chat part: with a group split off to its left (D2), the window's title row shows. |
| `c721992b08e` (P15b) | A part the grid creates or closes (D4, Move Editor into New Part) keeps the arrangement the window's, so Block 2 remembers its part sizes, unless something else, such as a part move, changed the arrangement first. |
| `e7fe6de271c` (P15) | Removed the now-unused `{ part, view }` cell shape (the chat is a plain part cell since Block 2's title-model rework). |
| `18c669eb186` (P14) | QA final FAIL #1: Move Part keeps the sizes of the other parts and the moved part takes the rest, so moving it back restores the layout (e.g. terminals stay 72px). |
| `d0c863be6ee` + `30737f51a01` (P16) | QA final FAIL #4: the groups of the chat part besides the chat's (an editor split into the chat part, D1a) are stored with the window (`IChatWindowOpenOptions.chatPart`: the part's state and the chat's group) and restored in place, with the chat back in its own group; a stored group the part no longer has falls back to the active group, and a stored value that is not one is ignored. |
| `4163c79626d` + `53c08b54fe9` (P15b) | Grid tests from the base pass the part factory and the editor groups service. |

## Decisions

- **Part drag handle: the card's top edge only** (user decision). No modifier on the title area: Alt already means copy / no-new-window on tab and group drags.
- **The chat drags by its session title only.** In a chat window the header sits in the title bar, whose empty space moves the OS window (`-webkit-app-region: drag`); that keeps working, and the title (`no-drag`) drags the chat.
- **The layout mode resets part moves** (user decision): a D3 move lasts until the next layout-mode change, which arranges the window again. Parts created by D4 stay across layout-mode changes until they close.
- **Webviews don't reload on part moves**: webviews render in an overlay, not inside the part's DOM (verified live).

title: grid: the maximum width of a grid view is its maximum width
body:
`GridView.maximumWidth` returned the root's `maximumHeight` instead of its `maximumWidth`.

**Why it went unnoticed:** every view's maximum size is normally unbounded (editors, etc.), so both values are `Infinity`. As soon as a view has a bounded maximum height, the grid reports that as its maximum width. Found in the chat windows work: a chat part showing only its input (Stacked) has a maximum height of 162, which made the chat and the main part only 164px wide.

**Fix:** return `this.root.maximumWidth`.

**Test:** new `gridview.test.ts` test adds a view with max width 700 / max height 100 and asserts `[maximumWidth, maximumHeight]` is `[700, 100]`. Without the fix it fails with `[100, 100]`.

title: Engineering - resubmit a macOS ESRP signing whose download stalls
body:
Some connections from Azure Storage to the ACES macOS agents run at about **0.2 MB/s** for as long as they're open (IcM 891066261, tracked in microsoft/vscode-engineering#4435). ESRP downloads each signed file on a single connection with no timeout, so a hit adds **25–40 minutes** to a macOS sign job. Since Oct 21 this has affected 7% of macOS ESRP downloads, including 8 of the last 11 official builds and the Nov 2 releasing insider.

## Change (macOS sign and notarize sessions only)

I decompiled EsrpCodeSigning 6.1.1 to confirm how it downloads (`SignCommand2.SaveFileWithDML`). It writes to `<file>.tmp`, verifies the SHA-256, and only then replaces the file. So the growth of the `.tmp` file is the download rate, and killing the session leaves the unsigned original in place.

`sign.ts` now runs macOS sessions under a download stall guard:
- **Detection:** every 15 s it records the size of the `.tmp` files for its pattern. If a file grew at less than **1 MB/s over the last 60 s**, the guard stops the session.
- **Recovery:** it removes the `.tmp` (ESRP opens it without truncating, so a leftover one would fail the hash check) and submits the file again. ESRP then downloads it on a new connection.
- **Limits:** at most **2 resubmissions**, after which the session runs to completion as it does today.
- **Settings:** `VSCODE_ESRP_DOWNLOAD_STALL_WINDOW_SECONDS` and `VSCODE_ESRP_DOWNLOAD_MIN_MB_PER_SECOND`.
- **Logging:** every trigger logs `[esrp-stall] type=… file=… rate=…MB/s window=…s attempt=n action=resubmit` plus a pipeline warning, so we can count triggers in our metrics.

A resubmission costs about 8–12 min (upload, sign and download), against 25–40 min for a stalled download. Each process signs exactly one file, so killing it affects only that file. Windows and Linux are unchanged.

**Thresholds:** across 876 macOS ESRP downloads over 50 MB since Sep 24, stalls averaged below 1 MB/s (60, all since Oct 21), and the healthy slow tail ran at 1.5–3 MB/s (86).

**Known limitation:** if ESRP retries a download after an exception, it rewrites the `.tmp` from the start without growing it. A retry lasting more than 60 s would therefore be treated as a stall and resubmitted. That costs one extra sign and doesn't fail anything.

## Validation

- `esrpDownloadStall.test.ts` adds 11 tests:
  - the stall window and rate
  - a healthy 1.5 MB/s download running to completion
  - a download that slows down partway
  - forgetting a finished download
  - matching `.tmp` files to the pattern, including the shared server folder
  - the guarded process being killed
  - All 19 tests pass, together with the existing Windows guard tests, and tsc is clean.
- **First forced-stall proof:** [492073](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=492073). The guard fired on all three macOS Sign jobs, but the resubmitted session failed with `Missing the encryption key data...`. esrpcli deletes the encryption key file after reading it (`GetEncryptionKeyData`), so `sign.ts` now writes a newly encrypted token for each session. The tests now include a fake esrpcli that consumes its key file the same way.
- **Forced-stall proof on the fixed head: [492138](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=492138) passed.** It used official insider parameters with Publish off.
  - On every macOS arch, the forced client codesign and notarize stalls were resubmitted, and each signed or notarized successfully. The run logged 8 `[esrp-stall]` lines.
  - `Verify signature` passed on all three arches, and `Create Universal App` passed.
  - The guard also caught **two real stalls** on the affected network:
    - x64 notarize DMG at 0.43 MB/s, resubmitted and done 6 min later
    - an arm64 codesign client resubmission at 0.18 MB/s. Its third session, which is unguarded, completed.
  - A resubmission costs one more full sign or notarize: 6–7 min for codesign and 10–15 min for notarize, against 25–40 min for a stalled download.
  - Windows and Linux sign jobs ran unchanged and passed.

title: CLI-installed canvas plugin loaded twice by local Copilot Agent Host (Written by Copilot)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: chat-customizations
labels.description: Instruction, agent, skill, and prompt files related issues

body:
Human tl;dr

I asked Copilot to install a plugin, it did this with the Copilot CLI. This seems like it should be ok. Then when I run the https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/345309 TPI steps, it fails, because I apparenlty ended up with two copies of the plugin present somehow, one from the CLI, one independently discovered by vscode.

---

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: N/A; this is the built-in Copilot Agent Host/runtime integration.
- VS Code Version: 1.145.0-insider, commit `67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff` (build date November 1, 2026).
- OS Version: macOS 26.7.1, arm64.
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Local Copilot Agent Host chat; canvas extension enablement.
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Not relevant to the failure; it occurs while an extension worker joins the session, before a model request.
- Logs: Sanitized excerpts below. Copilot SDK/platform package: `1.0.27-unstable.41214319014.g4f70995`. Plugin: `session-timeline` version `1.1.0`, from the `microsoft/vscode-team-kit` marketplace.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install a canvas-providing plugin through Copilot's native plugin installation path. The affected installation is `session-timeline@vscode-team-kit`:

   ```text
   /plugin marketplace add microsoft/vscode-team-kit
   /plugin install session-timeline@vscode-team-kit
   ```

   This creates an `installedPlugins` record in Copilot's config and installs the plugin under `$HOME/.copilot/installed-plugins/vscode-team-kit/session-timeline`.
2. Open a local Copilot Agent Host chat in VS Code. Let VS Code discover the installed plugin and synchronize its customizations to the host.
3. Ask the agent to show the session timeline, or invoke the plugin's `/session-timeline` skill, and leave the canvas open.
4. In the Canvases customization UI, disable the `session-timeline:session-timeline` canvas extension, then enable it again.
5. Observe the error below.

### Actual behavior

The UI reports:

```text
After enabling 'session-timeline:session-timeline', this chat couldn't finish updating canvas extensions because 'session-timeline:session-timeline' failed to start. This chat may not match your canvas extension settings.
```

The underlying worker failure is not specific to disabling a canvas while it is open. Logs also show the duplicate-loading failure during fresh chat startup.

### Expected behavior

The same installed plugin should not be loaded twice into the same local runtime. Disabling and reenabling its canvas extension should stop and restart one provider without a duplicate canvas registration.

### Worker logs: the same plugin starts from two directories in the same chat

At approximately 14:35:54 local time on November 2, the runtime launched both the original installed extension and VS Code's synchronized copy. Both workers had the same `SESSION_ID`. The two `extension.mjs` files were also compared locally and were byte-for-byte identical.

Paths and the session ID are normalized in these excerpts; no complete session logs are attached.

Original installed copy, worker PID 96647:

```text
=== launch pid=96647 module=$HOME/.copilot/installed-plugins/vscode-team-kit/session-timeline/com.github.copilot/extensions/session-timeline/extension.mjs ===
SESSION_ID=<same-chat-session-id>
=== initializing ===
[extension-bootstrap] Failed to load extension: Error: Request session.resume failed with message: Canvas "plugin:session-timeline:session-timeline/vscode-session-timeline" is already registered.
=== peer-closed-before-ready ===
=== exit code=1 disposition=startup-failure ===
```

VS Code's synchronized copy, worker PID 96648:

```text
=== launch pid=96648 module=$VSCODE_USER_DATA/agentPlugins/file-<original-plugin-path>/<revision>/com.github.copilot/extensions/session-timeline/extension.mjs ===
SESSION_ID=<same-chat-session-id>
=== initializing ===
=== ready ===
```

Corresponding Agent Host and runtime messages:

```text
2026-11-02 14:35:54.181 [warning] [Copilot:<same-chat-session-id>] Extension 'plugin:session-timeline:session-timeline' reconciliation reported a lifecycle failure Extension lifecycle reconciliation failed: extension did not become ready: plugin:session-timeline:session-timeline

2026-11-02T20:35:54.181Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::shared_api::plugins::reconciliation] extension reconciliation failed {"error":"Extension lifecycle reconciliation failed: extension did not become ready: plugin:session-timeline:session-timeline"}
```

An earlier attempt in the same chat had the opposite winner: the original worker PID 96488 reached `ready`, and the synchronized worker PID 96489 failed with the same `already registered` error. This is a collision between two concurrent copies, not just an old registration left behind after disabling the provider.

### Investigation

The observed behavior is consistent with the following loop:

1. Copilot's runtime discovers the native installation.
2. VS Code's `CopilotCliAgentPluginDiscovery` also discovers that installation so its contributions appear in the customization UI.
3. The shared client-customization pipeline forwards the plugin to the Agent Host. A materialized copy appears under VS Code's `agentPlugins` directory.
4. The local runtime receives that copy as an additional plugin directory while still discovering the native installation. Both extension workers try to register `plugin:session-timeline:session-timeline/vscode-session-timeline`.

Relevant VS Code paths:

- [CLI-installed plugin discovery](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/29aacc7fedf4975cd41d71c3a641a233ed1c73d4/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/plugins/agentPluginServiceImpl.ts#L1186-L1227).
- [Forwarding local plugin references](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/29aacc7fedf4975cd41d71c3a641a233ed1c73d4/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts#L250-L329). This deduplicates references by source URI, but does not exclude an installation already owned by the same local Copilot runtime.
- [Passing plugin directories to the SDK](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/29aacc7fedf4975cd41d71c3a641a233ed1c73d4/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts#L1720-L1721).

The integration needs to recognize the original installation and synchronized copy as the same plugin, or avoid forwarding an already-discovered installation back into the same local runtime. This should preserve synchronization to remote hosts and other providers that cannot discover the original installation. Suppressing the lifecycle error or changing this plugin's canvas ID would not address the duplicate loading.

### Related

- #345479 reports a similar native-discovery/client-forwarding duplication for custom agents. This report is specifically about duplicate canvas extension workers and the resulting startup/re-enable failure.
- An earlier, separate missing-plugin-directory error was resolved before capturing the failures above. These logs show an existing plugin failing on duplicate canvas registration, not a missing installation directory.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Permissions picker: locked sandbox switch and disabled Allow all don't expose their organization reason to keyboard/screen reader users

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: accessibility
labels.description: Keyboard, mouse, ARIA, vision, screen readers (non-specific) issues

body:
Keyboard and screen reader users can't find out why the permissions picker's policy-locked controls are locked. Mouse users see the reason on hover.

**Setup:** VS Code Insiders 1.145.0 (`67710841`), Linux. Managed settings at `/etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json` (macOS: `/Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/managed-settings.json`):

```json
{
  "permissions": { "disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable" },
  "sandbox": { "enabled": true, "allowBypass": false }
}
```

**Repro:**
1. Restart VS Code. In the Chat view, pick the **Copilot** harness.
2. Open the picker from the **Manual permissions** half of the chip. Opening it from **Interactive** collapses the Permissions section.
3. Use **Down Arrow** to move through the rows. **Tab** goes to the Configure Permissions gear, and a second Tab closes the picker.

**Actual:**

| Row | What a screen reader gets |
|---|---|
| Sandboxing for terminal (checked, locked) | `"Sandboxing for terminal, on"`. It doesn't say the switch is locked or why. |
| Allow all (disabled by policy) | Nothing. Down Arrow skips it, going straight from Assisted permissions to Sandboxing for terminal. Its row label also ends in a stray `"…, Disabled Reason: true"`. |

The reasons are in the DOM: the switch's own `aria-label` is "Sandboxing is required by your organization", and Allow all has an `ariaDescription`. But focus stays on the list's `role="menu"` and moves between rows with `aria-activedescendant`, so assistive tech reads only the row labels.

**Expected:** On the sandbox row, a screen reader hears something like "Sandboxing for terminal, on, unavailable. Sandboxing is required by your organization." Allow all can be focused, or its reason is reachable another way, and the stray "true" is gone.

![Keyboard focus on the locked sandbox row; its label is only "Sandboxing for terminal, on"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d89b3c85-2150-452b-bbda-e11dab498bc6)

![Down Arrow skips the disabled Allow all row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/374b028f-82aa-4b78-96b0-54cfe6c39302)

![Mouse users get both reasons from hovers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48ccac52-0017-43fc-a9ff-6acdca599520)

**Where it comes from** (all in [`actionList.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/actionWidget/browser/actionList.ts)):
- For standalone toggle rows, the [accessibility provider](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/actionWidget/browser/actionList.ts#L1199-L1207) *replaces* the row label with `"{label}, on|off"`. It drops `toggleConfig.title` and `toggleConfig.disabled`, which [are set](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/agentHostSandboxToggle.ts#L88) for the managed case. This came in with #330978.
- [`focusCondition`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/actionWidget/browser/actionList.ts#L1865) skips every `disabled` row. That's a reasonable default for quick fixes, but here it hides "visible but disabled, with a reason" rows that are meant to explain policy.
- [`"{0}, Disabled Reason: {1}"`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/actionWidget/browser/actionList.ts#L1210) interpolates `element.disabled`, which is now a `boolean`, so it reads "true".

None of these is new in 1.145. They surfaced in test plan item microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10486 (bug report microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10565). The sandbox-toggle and "your organization" wording changes it covered (#344670, #344835) didn't affect this path.

The Changes editor of the Agents window now shows the list of the changed files beside its diffs, as the workbench's multi diff editor can.

- The Changes editor hosts the workbench's `MultiDiffEditorWithFileListWidget`, in every window it shows in. The list shows unless the user hides it with **Toggle Files**. Hiding is remembered and shared with the multi diff editors. It doesn't depend on the experimental `multiDiffEditor.experimental.fileList` setting, which still gates the list of the workbench's multi diff editor.
- **Toggle Files** is the workbench's `multiDiffEditor.toggleFileList`, in the More Actions menu of the tab bar, after Collapse All Diffs, Word Wrap and Diff View. The Changes editor keeps no actions of its own in its header row.
- **Focus File List** and the accessibility help of the list apply to any editor that hosts the list (`IMultiDiffEditorFileListHost`), not only the workbench's multi diff editor.

This is a visible change to the Changes editor.

## Screenshots

Before: the Changes editor shows only the diffs.
After: the changed files list shows beside the diffs (default and compact density), and Toggle Files hides it.

(Screenshots: to be attached; captured from the dev build, before and after in default and compact density, and with the list hidden.)

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open a session with changes, then open its Changes editor: the changed files list shows beside the diffs, with `multiDiffEditor.experimental.fileList` off.
2. More Actions in the tab bar → Toggle Files: the list hides. Run it again: the list shows. The state survives a reload.
3. With focus in the Changes editor, run **Focus File List** from the Command Palette: focus moves into the list, which shows first if it was hidden.

## Validation

- New tests, failing without the change:
  - `SessionChangesEditor changed files list`: the list is shown with the experimental setting off, hidden by Toggle Files, and shown again by focusing it; the editor lays out the list.
  - `Multi diff editor file list of any host`: Focus File List focuses any host; the hidden state doesn't depend on the setting.

title: mcp: use URI-backed defaultCwd for home-directory discovery adapters
body:
Fixes #345646

The Claude Desktop, Copilot, Cursor and Windsurf native discovery adapters passed `{ cwd: homedir }` to `claudeConfigToServerDefinition`, which sets the stdio `launch.cwd` to `homedir.fsPath` on the client. On a Windows client connected to a Linux remote (e.g. WSL), this yields a Windows-style path (`\home\<user>`), and `spawn` on the Linux extension host fails with `ENOENT`.

This passes `{ defaultCwd: homedir }` instead, the same approach #330223 took for workspace `.mcp.json`. The cwd stays a URI and is resolved by the extension host. The cache nonce is still computed from `defaultCwd.fsPath`, so existing trust decisions are preserved.

A per-entry `cwd` in these files is still not read; that's unchanged and out of scope.

**Testing**
- Added a unit test covering all four adapters with a `vscode-remote://` home: stdio servers get no `launch.cwd`, `defaultCwd` is the home URI, and the nonce matches the previous behavior. The test fails without the fix.
- `node test/unit/node/index.js --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters.test.ts`: 13 passing.

title: MCP local (stdio) servers from ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json fail with spawn ENOENT on Windows client + Remote WSL

<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. But with WSL enabled because it is needed a a condition.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.144.0
- OS Version:  Windows 11 client, Remote WSL: openSUSE Tumbleweed

When VS Code runs on Windows and is connected to a Linux remote (Remote WSL in my case), local/stdio MCP servers discovered from `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` on the remote fail to start with `spawn <command> ENOENT`, even though the executable exists and runs fine from a WSL shell. The same server definitions start correctly when placed in the remote user `mcp.json`, and HTTP servers from `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` are not affected.

The cause appears to be the working directory VS Code assigns to these servers. The native discovery adapters set the launch `cwd` to the remote home directory converted to a path on the Windows client, which produces a Windows-style path (`\home\<user>`). On the Linux extension host that isn't a valid absolute directory, so Node's `spawn` fails with ENOENT. Node reports the error against the command, not the cwd, which makes it look like the executable is missing.

This is the same class of bug as #320167 (fixed for workspace `.mcp.json` by #330223), but the home-directory discovery adapters weren't covered by that fix. The Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Windsurf discovery sources share the same code path and are likely affected the same way.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On Windows, open VS Code and connect to a WSL distro using `WSL: Connect to WSL`.
2. In a WSL shell (Node.js installed inside WSL), install the reference MCP server into `~/.local`:
   ```sh
   npm install -g --prefix ~/.local @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything
   ls -l ~/.local/bin/mcp-server-everything
   ```
   Confirm it runs from the shell (it waits on stdin; exit with Ctrl+C):
   ```sh
   ~/.local/bin/mcp-server-everything
   ```
3. Create `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` in WSL:
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "everything": {
         "command": "/home/<user>/.local/bin/mcp-server-everything",
         "args": []
       }
     }
   }
   ```
4. In VS Code (connected to WSL), make sure Copilot config discovery is enabled in user settings (it's the default):
   ```json
   "chat.mcp.discovery.enabled": { "copilot": true }
   ```
5. Run `MCP: List Servers` from the Command Palette. `everything` is listed as discovered from `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`.
6. Select `everything`, choose `Start Server`, then `Show Output`.

**Expected:** the server starts and exposes its tools (e.g. `echo`).

**Actual:** the server fails to start:

```
Starting server from Remote extension host
Connection state: Error spawn /home/<user>/.local/bin/mcp-server-everything ENOENT
```

Retrying forced cleanup on a known leftover worktree whose previous removal attempt already unregistered it should finish removing the remaining directory rather than rejecting it.

title: Keep each window's idle sash grippers its own
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes the sash grippers of an auxiliary window of the Agents window disappearing for good while the mouse moves only in that window.

The three-dot sash grippers recede after the mouse has been idle in a window (`workbench.sash.autoHideGrippers`, 2s), and come back on the next mouse move in that window. Two defects broke this for auxiliary windows:

1. **The idle state was mirrored from the main window.** The auxiliary window service mirrors the class attribute of the main window's container onto each auxiliary window's container, on every change. The idle state was a class on that container (`sash-grippers-hidden`). While the mouse moves only in an auxiliary window, the main window goes idle, and its hidden state is copied into the auxiliary window. The idle state is now an attribute of each window's own container (`data-sash-grippers-hidden`), which is not mirrored; the core rule is `.monaco-workbench[data-sash-grippers-hidden] .monaco-sash`. The body and `<html>` are mirrored in full, so the state can't move there either.
2. **The Agents window never added auxiliary window containers.** Its workbench declares `onDidAddContainer` but never fired it, so `SashGrippersController`, and anything else that tracks every container, never tracked an auxiliary window opened after startup. It now fires it for every auxiliary window, as the standard workbench's layout does.

Together, an auxiliary window of the Agents window, such as an editor window, kept its grippers hidden while it was used, until the mouse moved in the main window again. This is a latent bug for any Agents window auxiliary window, and the cause of missing grippers in chat windows (behind `sessions.chatWindows.enabled`, #344666). The standard workbench's main window behaves as before.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open an auxiliary window, move the mouse once in the main window, then only in the auxiliary window for a few seconds: its grippers stay. Stop moving: they recede after 2s, and come back on the next move.
2. In a regular window: move the mouse, then stop for 2s: the grippers recede, and come back on the next move.

## Validation

- New tests, both failing without the fix:
  - `Sash grippers`: an auxiliary window keeps its own idle state while it mirrors the class of the main window's container.
  - `Sessions - Workbench`: adds the container of each auxiliary window that opens, and releases it with the window.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sash/test/browser/sash.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/test/browser/webviewElement.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionGridLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/workbench.test.ts`: 240 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/sessions/**/*.test.js"`: 9732 passing, 0 failing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/workbench/**/*.test.js"`: 28769 passing, 1 failing (`ChatListWidget` "falls back to a full refresh when the request or the transcript changes", which also fails on `main`).
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed. `pnpm run eslint <changed files>`: passed.
- Live (background, dev build), with `window.density.layout: compact` and `workbench.editor.showTabs: single`:
  - before: main idle, the mouse moving only in an auxiliary window of the Agents window: that window's container carried the hidden state and its grippers had opacity 0;
  - after: the same scenario: its grippers stay at opacity 1; it recedes after its own 2s idle and returns on its own mouse move;
  - regular workbench: recedes after 2s idle (`--sash-grip-opacity: 0` on every sash) and returns on the next move, as before.

title: Markdown editor Mermaid: removing markdown-mermaid.maxHeight is undone after toggling read/edit mode

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344532. That fix makes height cap *changes* reach open Markdown editors, and it works. But **removing** the cap only sticks until you switch between read and edit mode.

Found while verifying the fix on VS Code Insiders `1.145.0-insider` (commit `67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff`), Ubuntu 24.04 arm64.

## Repro

1. Create `mermaid.md` with a tall diagram:

   ````markdown
   ```mermaid
   flowchart TD
     S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> S5 --> S6 --> S7 --> S8 --> S9 --> S10
   ```
   ````

2. Open it with **Reopen Editor With… → Markdown Editor**. The diagram is uncapped.
3. Set `"markdown-mermaid.maxHeight": "150px"`. The diagram is capped right away. ✅
4. Remove the setting. The diagram is uncapped right away. ✅
5. Click the **lock** (read mode) or **pencil** (edit mode) toggle at the top right of the editor.

**Expected:** the diagram stays uncapped.

**Actual:** it's capped at the old 150px again, with an inner scrollbar. The Markdown preview beside it stays uncapped. Closing and reopening the editor clears it.

Possibly blocks re-created on a mode toggle reuse a cached presentation whose `maxAutomaticHeight` is still 150, because "no cap" (`undefined`) doesn't overwrite it. I haven't confirmed this. Low severity: the workaround is to reopen the editor.

## Screenshots and video

Removing the cap, then toggling read mode, brings the old 150px cap back. The preview stays uncapped.

```

npm notice run @repro/cli@0.0.0 hi
npm notice run node -e "console.log('hello from packages/cli')"
hello from packages/cli
```
Multi-root (`code .\repro.code-workspace`) — ROOT still runs through npm, but `packages/cli` is handed to
yarn:
```
yarn run hi
Internal Error: vscode-npm-scripts-yarn-repro@workspace:.: This package doesn't seem to be present in your lockfile; run "yarn install" to update the lockfile
    at jR.getCandidates (C:\Users\Administrator\.yarn\releases\yarn-4.12.0.cjs:204:4607)
    at rm.getCandidates (C:\Users\Administrator\.yarn\releases\yarn-4.12.0.cjs:141:1311)
    ...
```
Yarn is installed on this machine (4.12.0, under `~/.yarn/releases`), so the command exists — it just has
nothing to do with this project, and fails because there is no yarn lockfile to work from. On a machine
without yarn the same step simply never starts.
### What I expected
The repository decides which command runs, not the way the window was opened. Same folder, same
`package.json`, same lockfile → same command.
### Why I think it happens
`extensions/npm/src/tasks.ts` picks the runner from the workspace folder, while the command itself is run
in the package folder:
```ts
export async function createScriptRunnerTask(context, script, folder: WorkspaceFolder, packageJsonUri, ...) {
    const cwd = path.dirname(packageJsonUri.fsPath);                 // command runs in the package folder
    const args = await getRunScriptCommand(script, folder.uri, ...);  // detection uses the workspace folder
```
and `findPreferredPM()` in `preferred-pm.ts` does not look equally far for each manager:
| manager | evidence |
| --- | --- |
| npm | a `package-lock.json` in that exact folder |
| pnpm | local lockfile, or `findUp('pnpm-lock.yaml')` |
| yarn | local `yarn.lock`, or `find-yarn-workspace-root`, which walks up and treats any `package.json` with a `workspaces` field as a yarn workspace |
| bun | local lockfile |
Once `packages/cli` is a workspace root of its own, the root lockfile falls outside the folder being
checked, while the yarn heuristic still finds the parent `workspaces` field one level up. `workspaces` is
also exactly what npm workspaces uses, so on its own it doesn't tell us which manager is in play.
### One thing that cost me time
Most existing threads suggest `"npm.packageManager": "npm"`. That no longer decides which command runs a
script — `npm.scriptRunner` was split out for that — so it looks like the fix and quietly does nothing. I
only found this by reading the bundled extension.
### Related reports still open
I looked around first; these are the ones still open today:
| | opened | what it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [microsoft/vscode#170101](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/170101) | 2022-12-27 | `npm.packageManager=auto` assumes yarn |
| [microsoft/vscode#243250](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/243250) | 2025-03-11 | proposed fix for the detection |
| [microsoft/vscode#261630](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/261630) | 2025-08-14 | `npm.scriptRunner` auto-detection in subdirectories |
| [microsoft/vscode#302916](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/302916) | 2026-03-18 | proposed fix, prioritising the `packageManager` field |
| [microsoft/vscode#313218](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/313218) | 2026-04-29 | support `packageManager` in task detection |
The oldest has been open since December 2022, and the fix attempts from 2025 and 2026 are both still
waiting. None of them describes the part that surprised me here: the result also depends on whether the
folder is opened alone or as part of a multi-root workspace.
### Not asking for much
If this is how it is meant to work, a line saying so in the `npm.scriptRunner` description would have
saved me the detour. If it isn't, I'd be glad to test a build.

title: fix(linkedList): guard against removing disconnected nodes
body:
### Summary

In `LinkedList<E>` (`src/vs/base/common/linkedList.ts`):
- `_remove(node)` previously checked `else if (node.prev === Node.Undefined && node.next === Node.Undefined)` to detect the single-element list case, but did not verify `this._first === node`.
- When `clear()` is called on a list, detached nodes have their `prev` and `next` pointers set to `Node.Undefined`.
- If a removal callback (returned by `push()` or `unshift()`) associated with a node added prior to `clear()` was invoked after `clear()`, it matched the single-element branch. It then unconditionally cleared `this._first = Node.Undefined; this._last = Node.Undefined;` and decremented `this._size`.
- Consequently, if new elements had been inserted into the list after `clear()`, invoking that stale callback inadvertently destroyed active elements and corrupted `_size`.
- In addition, nodes removed via `_remove(node)` did not reset their `prev` and `next` pointers to `Node.Undefined`.

### Changes
1. Guard `_remove` early if `node === Node.Undefined`.
2. Check node identity (`this._first === node` and `this._last === node`) before clearing list endpoints or detaching boundary nodes.
3. Reset `node.prev` and `node.next` to `Node.Undefined` on removed nodes.
4. Add regression tests in `src/vs/base/test/common/linkedList.test.ts` covering stale callback invocations post-`clear()`, lower bound size guarantees, and idempotent removals.
