title: Agent Host: unsent drafts create real AHP sessions on remote hosts
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (fresh user data directory, no extensions installed)

- VS Code Version: 1.145.0-insider (67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff, 2026-11-01). Also reproduced on 1.144.0 (2c33b50b16).
- OS Version: macOS 27.2 (arm64)

## Summary

The Agents window sends `createSession` to a remote Agent Host for an unsent draft, before the
user sends anything. In AHP, `createSession` creates a session that the host announces to every
client with `root/sessionAdded`. VS Code's own Agent Host hides these drafts by withholding
`root/sessionAdded` (and `session/ready`) for "provisional" sessions until the first send. AHP
does not define that behavior. With a remote host that follows the spec, each unsent draft is a
real session. Other windows and clients list it as "New Session" for as long as the draft is open.

## AHP contract

- [Session lifecycle](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/ff7d6a1c7b4f5e47925d3ce1c3bcf685266a6d49/docs/specification/session-channel.md#L24-L31), step 8: "Server broadcasts root/sessionAdded to clients subscribed to ahp-root://"
- [`root/sessionAdded`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/ff7d6a1c7b4f5e47925d3ce1c3bcf685266a6d49/docs/specification/root-channel.md#L108-L110): "Emitted when a new session is created."
- [`resolveSessionConfig`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/ff7d6a1c7b4f5e47925d3ce1c3bcf685266a6d49/docs/specification/root-channel.md#L72): "Pre-creation config resolution happens before any session channel exists."

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a remote Agent Host in `chat.remoteAgentHosts`. The host must implement the documented `createSession` lifecycle. Then open the Agents window.
2. Choose that host under Environment and pick a folder. Do not type or send anything.
3. Open a second VS Code window with a separate user data directory, connect it to the same host, and open its Agents window.

## Actual

Raw messages from VS Code's AHP transport log (`chat.agentHost.ahpJsonlLoggingEnabled`).
Provider name, paths and large fields are elided.

Window A, after step 2:

```text
18:51:20.634 c2s {"method":"resolveSessionConfig","params":{"channel":"ahp-root://","provider":"<provider>","workingDirectory":"file:///path/to/workspace"}}
18:51:20.791 c2s {"method":"createSession","params":{"channel":"ahp-session:/aa33a68f-…","provider":"<provider>","workingDirectories":["file:///path/to/workspace"],"config":…,"activeClient":…}}
18:51:20.794 s2c {"method":"root/sessionAdded","params":{"summary":{"title":"New Session","status":1,…}}}
```

After **Developer: Reload Window**, window A creates another session with no user input:

```text
18:51:40.916 c2s {"method":"initialize",…}
18:51:41.218 c2s {"method":"resolveSessionConfig",…}
18:51:41.374 c2s {"method":"createSession","params":{"channel":"ahp-session:/49c5ca55-…",…}}
18:51:41.377 s2c {"method":"root/sessionAdded","params":{"summary":{"title":"New Session","status":1,…}}}
```

Window B never used that session, yet receives it from `listSessions` and lists it as
"New Session, updated 38 secs ago, State: Completed, unread":

```text
18:52:18.856 s2c {"id":3,"result":{"items":[{"title":"New Session","status":1,"createdAt":"2026-11-02T18:51:41.375Z",…}]}}
```

On 1.144.0, starting another new session disposes the previous draft and creates the next one.
Every client receives a `root/sessionRemoved`/`root/sessionAdded` pair each time. Closing or
reloading the window disposes the draft, so drafts do not persist. They are, however, real
listed sessions while the window is open.

## Expected

An unsent draft does not create an AHP session. VS Code already sends `resolveSessionConfig`.
The documented pre-creation flow, `resolveSessionConfig` and `sessionConfigCompletions`, covers
the draft's configuration. `createSession({ config, … })` can then run on the first send.

## Source references (at the tested Insiders build, 67710841)

- [agentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService.ts L22–L23](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService.ts#L22-L23): `getOrCreate` "creates a backend provisional session so `SessionConfigChanged` actions have a reducer-owned `SessionState`". The `createSession` call is at [L709](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService.ts#L709).
- [agentService.ts L6397–L6399](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L6397-L6399): "Provisional sessions do not emit `sessionAdded` or `SessionReady` until `onDidMaterializeChat`"
- [agent.ts L263–L271](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agent.ts#L263-L271): the `provisional` flag is used "to defer the `sessionAdded` protocol notification"

Related, not a duplicate: #332831 (the same provisional mechanism withholds `session/ready`).

title: fix(arrays): handle empty and out-of-bounds states in ArrayQueue
body:
### Summary

In `ArrayQueue<T>` (`src/vs/base/common/arrays.ts`):
- `dequeue()` on an empty queue previously incremented `this.firstIdx` without checking if elements were available, causing `firstIdx > lastIdx + 1`. Consequently, `this.length` was computed as a negative number (`-1`, `-2`, etc.).
- `removeLast()` on an empty queue similarly decremented `this.lastIdx` without checking `this.length`.
- Because `peek()` and `peekLast()` guard with `if (this.length === 0)`, a negative length bypassed the empty guard and attempted out-of-bounds indexing.
- `takeCount(count)` did not bound `count` to available elements, causing `firstIdx` to overshoot `lastIdx + 1` when `count > this.length`, while negative counts triggered unintended array slicing.

### Changes
1. Return `undefined` early from `dequeue()` and `removeLast()` when `this.length === 0`.
2. Return `[]` from `takeCount(count)` when `count <= 0` or `this.length === 0`, and clamp `count` to `Math.min(count, this.length)`.
3. Ensure `get length()` always returns non-negative values via `Math.max(0, this.lastIdx - this.firstIdx + 1)`.
4. Add regression unit tests in `src/vs/base/test/common/arrays.test.ts` verifying empty and boundary behaviors for `dequeue()`, `removeLast()`, `peek()`, `peekLast()`, and `takeCount()`.

title: Agent Host sustains high CPU with repeated session catalog reconciliation/database opens

body:
CPU is running very hot, copilot says it's from heavy session processing.

## Summary

VS Code Insiders' Agent Host sustains high CPU while repeatedly processing the same session catalogs. The machine is running hot without comparable editor/language-server activity.

- Build: `67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff` (Windows ARM64, 12 logical processors).
- Agent Host PID 39192: approximately **18% total-machine CPU**, equivalent to **2.1–2.2 CPU cores**, across multiple samples. It remained at **17.7% / 2.13 cores after the debugger detached**.
- In a **12.1-second** log window: **1,398 `kind=migration, stage=started` operations across 49 distinct sessions** and **6,838 session database opens**. Some individual sessions appeared 31 times.
- One I/O sample for Agent Host: approximately **15.8 MB/s reads**, **1.3 MB/s writes**, and **6,835 I/O operations/s**.

## CPU profile / implicated code

A 12.41-second V8 CPU profile (7,720 samples) shows session catalog/database and identity-translation work:

| Function | Profile observation | Source at installed build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SessionStorageIdentity._record` | 228 ms self / 682 ms total | [sessionStorageIdentity.ts:208](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionStorageIdentity.ts#L208) |
| `readSessionListCatalogs` | 486 ms total | [compatibleAgentHostDatabase.ts:381](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/compatibleAgentHostDatabase.ts#L381) |
| `tryOpenDatabase` | 426 ms total | [sessionDataService.ts:132](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/67710841ad061a9e253214f87bf5415a185ab2ff/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionDataService.ts#L132) |

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Summary

Let an agent mark the session it is running in as Done. Apply the archive when the current turn ends, the way `set_workspace` applies its change after the turn.

This is the agent-tool counterpart of #292426, which asks for a Mark as Done button in the conversation for the user. It extends #344861 rather than repeating it.

## Current behavior

#344861 added the `archive_chat` server tool. It archives another chat or session, and deliberately refuses the chat it runs in and the main session of its own session, so an agent cannot archive the conversation that is calling it. That refusal makes sense for an immediate archive.

## Problem

The most common time an agent should mark a session Done is at the end of that same session. A wrap-up workflow, such as a `/done` skill, checks for uncommitted work, stops helper processes, and summarizes follow-ups. Its last step is to mark the session Done, and that is the one step it cannot take: it has to ask the user to find the session in the Sessions list and click Mark as Done.

## Proposal

When `archive_chat` targets the chat it runs in or its own session, schedule the archive instead of refusing:

- The tool result tells the model to end the turn, as `set_workspace` does.
- When the turn completes, the host archives the target with the same validation and side effects as archiving from the UI, including the worktree commit and cleanup for isolated sessions.
- If the turn fails or is cancelled, or a queued message is waiting to start another turn, the scheduled archive is dropped.

Archiving keeps history and can be undone, so this needs no more confirmation than `archive_chat` has today.

## Alternatives considered

- Ask the user to click Mark as Done: works today, and is the extra step this request removes.
- Have a second session call `archive_chat` on this one: leaves the second session needing the same click, and races the turn that is still running.
- `delete_session`: refuses the current session, cannot be undone, and removes history.

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Summary

We're considering deferring `add_artifact_or_reference` behind tool search in Agent Host Copilot SDK sessions, so its definition stops being sent on every request. Telemetry shows recorded artifacts are rarely opened, especially files. Details are in microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10562.

Before we can do that, there's a dependency on restricted PR association (#335161). With `chat.agentHost.experimental.autoAttachPullRequests` at its default `false`, a PR the **agent** creates (for example with `gh pr create` in a shell, or a GitHub `create_pull_request` tool) is associated with the session only if the model also records it with `add_artifact_or_reference`:

- `AgentHostPullRequestAssociationResolver._getRestrictedCandidates` limits candidates to PR artifacts (`getPullRequestArtifactUrls`) plus `associatedPullRequestUrls`.
- `associateRecordedPullRequests` is called from the artifact tool (`artifactServerTools.ts`).
- PRs created through the Create PR action (`agentHostPullRequestOperationProvider.ts`) and sessions started from a PR (`agentService._buildInitialSummary`) are recorded by the host and don't need the tool.

If the tool is deferred, the model will rarely call it unprompted. Model-created PRs would then silently lose the PR pill, status, Mark Ready, Merge and Agent Merge in restricted mode.

## Options

1. **The host records a PR artifact when it observes the agent creating a PR.** For example, a shell tool call whose command is `gh pr create` and whose output contains the PR URL, or a GitHub MCP `create_pull_request` result. The host would record what the agent created on its behalf, so restricted-mode semantics stay the same: only agent-recorded PRs. This could be implemented as an agent-host chat contribution observing completed tool calls. Tool names and inputs differ by provider, so it could start with Copilot SDK sessions, which is where the deferral would apply.
2. **The host treats a PR on the session's own head branch, created after the session started, as agent-recorded.** This needs no tool parsing and works for every provider, but it narrows the difference between the experiment arms.
3. **Keep the tool eager** and narrow its description so it only records PRs and issues the agent creates, never files. This cuts most unprompted calls but keeps paying for the definition on every request.

@benibenj since you own restricted association and the auto-attach experiment, which approach would you prefer? I'm happy to implement option 1.

## Related

- microsoft/vscode#338589: eval of artifact reminder cost
- microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10562: artifact open telemetry analysis

title: chat.agent.sandbox.enabled: "off"` is saved and correctly propagated to `agent-host-config.json`, but the agent's spawned terminal process remains sandboxed (AppContainer)
body:
**Environment:**
- VS Code version: 1.144.0 (commit `2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf`, x64)
- OS: Windows 11, build 26200 (25H2)
- GitHub Copilot Chat extension: 0.45.1

**Summary:**
The agent terminal remains confined to a Windows AppContainer sandbox even though every layer of configuration I can inspect confirms sandboxing should be off. This blocks any workflow requiring interactive MSAL/Azure AD sign-in (which needs to bind a local loopback `HttpListener` to catch the OAuth redirect) or access to the real (non-virtualized) user profile/token cache.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Set `"chat.agent.sandbox.enabled": "off"` in user `settings.json`.
2. Confirm `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Code\User\globalStorage\agent-host-config.json` correctly shows `"sandbox": {"enabled": "off", ...}` (it does — config propagation itself works correctly).
3. In an agent chat session, run a PowerShell tool-call command:
   ```powershell
   Write-Host "LOCALAPPDATA: $env:LOCALAPPDATA"
   try { $l = New-Object System.Net.HttpListener; $l.Prefixes.Add("http://localhost:48593/"); $l.Start(); Write-Host "LISTENER: OK"; $l.Stop() } catch { Write-Host "LISTENER: FAILED - $($_.Exception.Message)" }
   Get-Process | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count
   ```

**Expected:** `LOCALAPPDATA` resolves to the real user path; the listener binds successfully; the full host process list is visible (sandbox genuinely off).

**Actual:** Every single time:
- `LOCALAPPDATA` resolves to a virtualized path: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Packages\sandbox.{random-guid}\AC` — a **new GUID on every invocation**, suggesting a fresh AppContainer assignment per process/session rather than one stale cached container.
- `HttpListener.Start()` throws `Access is denied`.
- `Get-Process` only returns 3 processes total (`conhost`, `Idle`, the shell itself) — consistent with AppContainer process-list isolation.

**What I've already tried, all producing the identical sandboxed result:**
1. Editing `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` to `"off"` directly in `settings.json`.
2. Confirming (by inspecting `agent-host-config.json`) that the change is correctly read and live-applied — the log file `agenthost.log` shows `"Applied SDK sandboxConfig via session.options.update"` immediately after each `settings.json` save, with no reload needed.
3. A full VS Code window reload.
4. **A full OS reboot** taken *after* the setting was already saved (ruling out a stale pre-boot cache as the cause).
5. The in-chat **`/sandbox disable`** slash command — the chat responds "Sandboxing has been disabled," but the very next tool-call command still shows all three sandboxed fingerprints above, completely unchanged.

**Additional data point:** The sandbox block in `agent-host-config.json` also already has `"allowUnsandboxedCommands": true` set (independent of `enabled`), which based on its name should presumably bypass sandboxing outright, but it appears to have no observable effect either.

**Hypothesis:** The AppContainer assignment may happen once per agent-host process lifetime (or be cached at a layer above the per-session `sandboxConfig` object), so none of the "live" config-update paths I tried — `settings.json` edit, `/sandbox disable`, or even an OS reboot — actually reach the code path responsible for AppContainer assignment on newly spawned terminal processes. I was not able to isolate a full quit-and-relaunch of VS Code (distinct from "reload window") as a separate test, in case that specific action is relevant.

**Impact:** This makes it impossible to run interactive Azure AD/MSAL sign-ins (and likely any workflow needing a local listener or the real, non-virtualized user profile) from within an agent session, forcing a fully manual hand-off workaround (user runs the same commands themselves, outside the agent) for any task requiring fresh interactive authentication.

title: False positive: "agent tool must be included in tools" warning when agent/runSubagent is listed instead of the toolset alias
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (reproduces in core — `promptValidator.ts` is part of the workbench, not an extension)

- VS Code Version: 1.144.0 (Commit 2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf)
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create an agent file (`.agent.md`) with frontmatter containing both `tools` and `agents`, where `tools` lists the individual tool `agent/runSubagent` (not the bare alias `agent`), e.g.:

   ```yaml
   tools: ['agent/runSubagent', 'read/readFile']
   agents: ['SomeSubagent']
   ```

2. Open the file and observe the Problems panel / diagnostics for the agent file.

**Expected:** No warning — `agent/runSubagent` is the tool through which the `agent` toolset's subagent-dispatch capability is exposed, and is sufficient to invoke subagents.

**Actual:** The following warning is reported:

> When 'agents' and 'tools' are specified, the 'agent' tool must be included in the 'tools' attribute.

## Root cause

[`validateAgentsAttribute` in `promptValidator.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f44e32d2615ab314618f2be1b0eb677ec6570728/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptValidator.ts#L1417) does a literal string comparison:

```ts
if (agentNames.length > 0) {
    const tools = header.tools;
    if (tools && !tools.includes(SpecedToolAliases.agent)) {
        report(toMarker(localize('promptValidator.agentsRequiresAgentTool', "When 'agents' and 'tools' are specified, the 'agent' tool must be included in the 'tools' attribute."), attribute.value.range, MarkerSeverity.Warning));
    }
}
```

`SpecedToolAliases.agent` resolves to the literal string `'agent'` (defined in [`languageModelToolsService.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f44e32d2615ab314618f2be1b0eb677ec6570728/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts)'s `SpecedToolAliases` namespace) — this is the *toolset alias*, not an individual tool name. `tools.includes('agent')` only matches the literal alias string, not `agent/runSubagent`, which is the actual (and currently only) tool through which the `agent` toolset's capability is exposed in frontmatter.

### Why this is a bug, not intended behavior

Elsewhere in the same validator (`validateVSCodeTools`, `validateCopilotTools`), tool/toolset resolution goes through proper resolvers (`toToolAndToolSetEnablementMap`, `resolveAgentFileToolIdentifiers`) that understand toolset membership. `validateAgentsAttribute` is the exception — it does a naive string-equality check instead of checking "is the `agent` toolset enabled, or is any individual tool belonging to it listed?"

### Suggested fix

Resolve toolset membership the same way `validateVSCodeTools`/`validateCopilotTools` do (e.g. via `toToolAndToolSetEnablementMap`), instead of exact string equality against the toolset alias `'agent'`. At minimum, also accept the literal `agent/runSubagent` tool name — today the only tool in that namespace — and ideally match any future tool prefixed `agent/` so the check doesn't need updating again if more tools are added to that toolset.

title: HTML: resolve relative links only against hierarchical base URIs
body:
The HTML server's `resolveReference` resolved relative hrefs against any `<base href>`. With a non-hierarchical base, a relative href took over the base's scheme and query, producing document links whose scheme the language service would otherwise filter out.

Relative references are now only resolved against `http`, `https`, `file` or the document's own scheme. Any other base yields no link, which `DocumentContext.resolveReference` allows (`string | undefined`).

## How to test
- `cd extensions/html-language-features/server && pnpm run test` → 72 passing, including the new `Only resolves relative references against hierarchical bases`.
- Manually in Code OSS:
  - With `<base href="command:...">`, a relative href is no longer a link.
  - A relative link without `<base>` still opens the target file.
  - An `https:` `<base>` still resolves, e.g. `https://example.com/docs/guide/page.html?q=1`.
- ESLint on the changed files passes.

title: Fix backslash escaping in MarkdownString.appendLink
body:
`MarkdownString.appendLink` considered a `)`, `]` or `"` delimiter escaped whenever it directly followed a backslash. With an even run of backslashes (e.g. `\\)`), Markdown pairs the backslashes and the delimiter stays active, so the link target could end the generated link early.

Changes:
- `MarkdownString._escape` treats a delimiter as escaped only after an odd number of backslashes, and completes a trailing odd backslash run so it cannot escape the closing delimiter that `appendLink` adds.
- The editor link hover no longer marks the whole hover as trusted. A `command:` link only enables the command it targets (`enabledCommands`); other links render untrusted.

## How to test
- Unit tests: `scripts/test --run src/vs/base/test/common/markdownString.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/browser/markdownRenderer.test.ts` → 196 passing, 2 pending. The two new tests fail without the `_escape` change.
- Manually in Code OSS: an HTML `href` containing `\\)` followed by more Markdown link syntax now shows a single "Follow link" whose target is the whole URL.
- An extension-provided `command:` document link still runs from the hover and on Ctrl+click.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` and ESLint on the changed files pass.

title: Copilot cannot recover when a failing PermissionRequest hook blocks all tools
body:
## Type of issue
Bug

## Environment
- VS Code: 1.144.0 (x64)
- OS: Windows
- Copilot agent with Claude-compatible workspace hooks enabled

## Problem
A failing `PermissionRequest` hook loaded from `.claude/settings.json` caused every Copilot tool operation that required permission to fail with:

```
Permission denied by a PermissionRequest hook: Permission request hook failed
```

This included terminal commands, file edits, test execution, tool discovery, and even attempts to edit or disable the failing hook itself. The workspace was therefore stuck in a recovery deadlock until the hook configuration was repaired outside Copilot and VS Code was reloaded.

## Reproduction
1. Enable Claude-compatible hooks for Copilot.
2. Add a `PermissionRequest` command hook under `.claude/settings.json` that exits unsuccessfully or cannot launch (for example, because it depends on a Claude-specific environment variable or incompatible command shape).
3. Start a Copilot agent session in that workspace.
4. Ask Copilot to run a command or edit a file.
5. Try to have Copilot repair or remove the failing hook.

## Actual behavior
Every permission-gated tool is denied because the permission hook itself failed. Copilot cannot edit the hook that caused the denial. Reloading the window alone is insufficient until the file is repaired by another editor/agent.

## Expected behavior
A hook execution failure should not create an unrecoverable workspace deadlock. One or more of these recovery behaviors would help:

- Fall back to the normal permission prompt when a `PermissionRequest` hook crashes.
- Offer a safe-mode action to disable workspace hooks for the current session.
- Allow editing the hook configuration that caused the failure.
- Clearly identify the hook file and command that failed in the error UI.

A deliberate hook decision to deny should remain enforceable; this report is specifically about hook infrastructure/command failure, not an intentional denial.

title: TypeScript: resolve Node from PATH when detecting the TS Server Node
body:
When `js/ts.tsserver.node.path` (or `typescript.tsserver.nodePath`) is set to `node`, the TS extension detects a Node installation by spawning the bare command `node`. On Windows, a bare command name is also looked up in the current working directory before `PATH`, and the detection used the first workspace folder as its working directory.

This change resolves `node` to an absolute path using only the fully qualified `PATH` entries (drive-letter or UNC paths on Windows; relative entries such as `.` are skipped) and spawns that absolute path. The workspace folder is still used as the working directory for trusted workspaces, so version manager shims can pick the project's Node version. Explicitly configured absolute Node paths are unchanged.

- `extensions/typescript-language-features/src/utils/findExecutable.electron.ts`: new `findExecutableOnPath` helper.

### Description

In the **normal VS Code editor window**, several Copilot CLI-backed sessions containing child/forked chats repeatedly appear unread after restarting VS Code, despite opening the conversations and explicitly using **Mark as Read** or **Mark All as Read**.

The UI can show a session as read while the Agent Host session listing and persisted database state still report unread. The affected sessions are idle; no new assistant activity is required.

### Environment

- UI: normal VS Code editor window, **not** the separate Agents window.
- Session provider: Copilot CLI-backed Agent Host.
- Remote VS Code Server: **1.144.0**, stable, Linux x64.
- Server commit: `2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf`.
- Server build date: `2026-10-27T20:18:03Z`.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed with several existing sessions containing a main conversation and a child/fork:

1. Open both conversations.
2. Use **Mark All as Read**, or explicitly mark the parent session read.
3. Observe that the UI considers the session read.
4. Close and reopen VS Code.
5. The session appears unread again, without new assistant activity.

A fresh-session reproduction has not yet been verified.

### Expected

Explicitly marking a session read should survive refresh and restart.

If unread children intentionally prevent the parent from being read, the editor should expose a working way to clear their unread state rather than present a successful read state that does not persist.

### Diagnostic evidence

With Agent Host logging set to Trace, I explicitly toggled one affected **parent** session unread, then read.

On **2026-11-02**, times **UTC-05:00**:

| Time | Request received by Agent Host | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 09:59:06.454 | `session/isReadChanged`, `isRead: false` | Acknowledged and broadcast |
| 09:59:10.620 | `session/isReadChanged`, `isRead: true` | Acknowledged and broadcast |

No corresponding `chat/isReadChanged` events for that session's main or child chat appeared in the captured toggle window.

Read-only queries of the central `agent-host.db` showed:

| Stored value | Before toggle | Approximately 27 seconds after "read" acknowledgement |
|---|---|---|
| Session `isRead` | Empty string / unread | Empty string / unread |
| Main chat `chats_v2.is_read` | `0` | `0` |
| Child chat `chats_v2.is_read` | `0` | `0` |
| Main chat `metadata_revision` | `241` | `241` |
| Child chat `metadata_revision` | `18` | `18` |

No explicit read-state persistence error was found in the captured trace.

These snapshots do **not** establish whether the parent flag was never persisted as read or was briefly persisted and then overwritten.

### Possible investigation area

The parent-level read request reaches the host, but the individual chat records remain unread. This suggests a parent/child read-state synchronization or reconciliation issue; the exact faulty component is not yet established.

Possibly related:

- [#340103 - single-chat sessions revert to unread in the Agents window](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/340103). That report affects single-chat sessions in the separate Agents window, with the main chat already read and multi-chat sessions unaffected. This reproduction affects sessions with children in the normal editor window: both main and child chat records remain unread, and the host acknowledges `session/isReadChanged(isRead: true)` without corresponding chat-level read updates. The symptoms may share underlying synchronization logic, but an identical root cause has not been established.
- [#310884 - sessions become unread when reopening the window](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/310884).
- [#344128 - promoted nested chat repeatedly becomes unread](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344128). Unlike that report, these sessions still contain their children; promotion is not a reproduction step.

Session databases were inspected read-only, not modified. Raw logs and databases are omitted because they contain private conversation data.

title: askQuestions long question descriptions cause awkward nested scrolling and layout
body:
### Description

When an agent invokes `vscode/askQuestions` with long question descriptions in the Agents Window, the question carousel renders an awkward nested scrollable region.

The description occupies a large fixed-height area with its own scrollbar, while the question title appears immediately below it and is also displayed again in the answer section.

This makes the question UI visually cluttered and difficult to read, especially when the agent asks multiple questions.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the VS Code Agents Window.
2. Start an agent session using GitHub Copilot.
3. Have the agent invoke `vscode/askQuestions` with multiple questions (e.g. six), including a question with a lengthy description.
4. Observe the rendered question carousel.

### Actual Behavior

- Long question descriptions are displayed inside a constrained, independently scrollable area.
- The question title appears directly against the bottom edge of the scrollable description, creating an apparent clipping or overlap.
- The same question title is repeated in the answer section.
- The resulting layout makes it difficult to distinguish the description, question, and answer controls.

### Expected Behavior

- Long descriptions should be clearly separated from question titles and answer controls.
- Text should not appear clipped or visually crowded at scroll-container boundaries.
- Question titles should not be unnecessarily duplicated.
- The question carousel should handle lengthy descriptions gracefully.
